ExtraSection.description: A section of a living specification outside its template, kept as prose and not validated.

heading.description: The heading of the section, as written; not empty.

text.description: The content of the section, as written; absent when the section has no content.

OpenQuestion.description: An open question of a living specification.

id.description: Identifier within the specification, `Q<k>`, when the question has one.

text.description: The question, and its answer once resolved.

Requirement.description: An EARS requirement of a living specification.

id.description: Identifier within the specification, `R<k>`, never used again.

name.description: Short name, changed by a rename.

status.description: Whether the requirement is in force; absent means `active`, which is not a default applied by the engine.

RequirementStatus.description:
Status of a requirement within its living specification.

- `active`: In force.
- `removed`: Removed by a change delta; kept so that its identifier is never used again.

SpecCriterion.description: An acceptance criterion of a living specification.

id.description: Identifier within the specification, `AC<k>`, cited as `SPEC-<seq> AC<k>`.

requirements.description: The active requirements of this specification it verifies; at least one.

items.description: Identifier of a requirement of a living specification: `R` and a number from 1 without a leading zero, for example `R2`.

rubric.description: Rubric of the judge; required when `verification` contains `judge`.

verification.description: Verification techniques; at least one. The order of the values and a value repeated carry no meaning.

SpecificationStatus.description:
Status of a living specification (SPEC-0001 R5); `draft` and `surveyed` are its initial statuses.

- `draft`: Written, not approved.
- `approved`: Approved by a person; tasks may cite it.
- `surveyed`: Written by the survey of an existing project (SPEC-0011 R4), not approved.
- `implementing`: A task that cites it is claimed.
- `done`: Delivered, as a person declares; terminal.
- `superseded`: Replaced by the specifications in `superseded_by`; terminal.

Verification.description:
A verification technique of a task or of an acceptance criterion (SPEC-0009 R7).

- `tdd`: Test-driven development: a test written before the code.
- `bdd`: Behaviour-driven development: a scenario in the language of the user.
- `end_to_end`: A test of the whole system, through its interface.
- `property`: A property test over generated inputs.
- `contract`: A contract test against a published schema or case.
- `benchmark`: A measurement against a stated threshold.
- `judge`: A judgement against a rubric, which is then required (SPEC-0009 R8).
- `none`: Verified by no technique, stated on purpose.

description: A living specification (SPEC-0001, Living specification): the current behaviour of one capability (ADR 0014), in the normalised form of its file `specs/<NNNN>-<capability>/spec.md`.

acceptance_criteria.description: The acceptance criteria; at least one.

capability.description: The capability described, the slug of the folder.

commit_scope.description: Scope of the project policy used by the commits that implement it.

extra_sections.description: Sections outside the template; `[]` means none.

id.description: Stable identifier, in the canonical form of the type; assigned by the engine and never reused (SPEC-0001 R2, R14).

interfaces.description: Commands, schemas and events, with their versions; `[]` means none.

items.description: A prose text of at least one character, in the language of the document.

language.description: Language of the prose, a BCP 47 tag; when absent, the language of the project.

open_questions.description: Open and resolved questions; `[]` means none.

related.description: Identifiers of ADRs, issues and specifications, as written, for example `ADR 0014`; `[]` means none.

items.description: A prose text of at least one character, in the language of the document.

requirements.description: The requirements, removed ones included; at least one.

schema_version.description: Version of the schema of the type the document was written against (SPEC-0001 R16).

scope_in.description: What is specified; at least one entry.

items.description: A prose text of at least one character, in the language of the document.

scope_out.description: What is left to other specifications; `[]` means nothing.

items.description: A prose text of at least one character, in the language of the document.

status.description: Current status (SPEC-0001 R5), not the issue-cycle state of SPEC-0002.

stories.description: Stories covered, by identifier; `[]` means none.

items.description: Identifier of a user story: `STORY-` and four digits, or five or more without a leading zero, for example `STORY-0042`.

superseded_by.description: Identifiers of the artifacts of the same type that replace this one, at least one; required when `status` is `superseded`.

items.description: Identifier of a living specification: `SPEC-` and four digits, or five or more without a leading zero, for example `SPEC-0003`.

title.description: Outcome or name, in sentence case without a final full stop; 1 to 120 characters (Unicode code points).

user_stories.description: Stories written as prose, before or without a story artifact; `[]` means none.

items.description: A prose text of at least one character, in the language of the document.
